identificationModule.officialTitle: Phase I Clinical Study of CAR-T Cells (C-4-29) in the Treatment of Patients With Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma

descriptionModule.detailedDescription: This is a multi-center, single-arm, open-label study. The study plans to set up 3 dose groups, adopting a dose-escalating 3+3 design, and plan to recruit about 9-18 subjects with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.C-4-29 cells will be infused to the subject by intravenous infusion.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Incidence of Adverse events after C-4-29 infusion [Safety and Tolerability]
primaryOutcomes.description: Therapy-related adverse events were recorded and assessed according to the National Cancer Institute's Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE, Version 5.0)

primaryOutcomes.measure: Obtain the maximum tolerated dose of C-4-29 cells[Safety and Tolerability]

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Objective response rate after C-4-29 infusion [Effectiveness]
secondaryOutcomes.description: Objective response rate includes sCR, CR, VGPR, PR, MR
AUCS is defined as the area under the curve in 28 days
CMAX is defined as the highest concentration of C-4-29 cells expanded in peripheral blood
TMAX is defined as the time to reach the highest concentration

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Peripheral blood M protein contents after C-4-29 infusion [Cell dynamics]
secondaryOutcomes.description: Periodic detection of Peripheral blood M protein after cell infusion

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Urine Bence-Jones protein contents after C-4-29 infusion [Cell dynamics]
secondaryOutcomes.description: Periodic detection of Urine Bence-Jones protein after cell infusion

otherOutcomes.description: OS is defined as the time from C-4-29 cell infusion to death due to any cause
PFS is defined as the time from the start of the C-4-29 infusion to the first disease progression or death from any cause

otherOutcomes.measure: Duration of relief after C-4-29 infusion
otherOutcomes.description: DOR is defined as the time from reaching MR or better to disease progression or death from any cause
